sn.c: The Mezzanine overhang starts at row L, and from row R back it cuts noticeably into the top of the stage.
sn.sh: Overhang cuts into the top of the stage

sn.c: Seats toward the outside aisles of the Left and Right Orchestra have partial views of the stage.
sn.sh: Outside aisle seats have partial views

sn.c: Thin support poles near the aisles between Balcony rows C and D cut through the view for some seats behind them.
sn.sh: Thin support poles near the aisles

sn.lo: Center Mezzanine, rows E to G
sn.c: Center Mezzanine rows E to G are good value, with elevated and mostly clear views.
sn.sh: Elevated, mostly clear views for less

sn.c: Row A of the Center Balcony is high but mostly clear, and one of the less expensive seats in the house.
Raised boxes on each side of the Orchestra hold 16 people in total and give angled views of the stage.
The Balcony is very steep with cramped legroom, so hold the handrails on the way to your seat.

vs.sum: The Shubert Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, though some seats may require leaning forward for a full view. The sound quality is generally consistent and clear. While legroom is limited in some areas, the theater's historic charm and central location add to its appeal. Facilities are average, with typical lines at restrooms and concessions.

acc.note: 7 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No wheelchair-accessible restrooms (available across street).

vr.q: There is definitely a lot to love about this show, especially the performances by Joy Woods and Jeremy Kushnier.
